items.title: V Bratislavě se konaly Open Talks
items.summary: V úterý 20. října se pod záštitou slovenského Úradu na ochranu osobných údajov v Bratislavě uskutečnilo setkání Open Talks. Zástupci profesních asociací pověřenců a dozorových úřadů porovnávali zkušenosti z Česka, Slovenska, Polska, Maďarska a Rakouska.

items.title: Handhavingsbeleid AP gepubliceerd
items.summary: De Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (AP) heeft het handhavingsbeleid openbaar gemaakt. Dit beleid gaat over de inzet van handhavingsinstrumenten als organisaties zich niet aan de privacyregels houden.

items.title: AP informeert incassobureaus over verantwoorde inzet AI
items.summary: Incassobureaus gebruiken steeds vaker algoritmes en AI, zo blijkt uit een steekproef van de Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (AP) onder 29 bureaus. Het werk gaat hierdoor sneller, maar het leidt ook tot risico’s op onjuiste beslissingen, discriminatie en ongelijke behandeling. Om verkeerd gebruik van computersystemen te helpen voorkomen, komt de AP met aanbevelingen aan de incassosector.

items.title: AP onderzoekt websites vanwege misleidende cookiebanner
items.summary: De Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (AP) is een onderzoek gestart naar 2 organisaties die een misleidende cookiebanner blijven gebruiken op hun website, ondanks uitleg en een waarschuwing van de AP. De cookiebanner van deze organisaties heeft geen direct zichtbare knop waarmee websitebezoekers volgsoftware (trackingcookies) kunnen weigeren. Hierdoor zullen bezoekers eerder trackingcookies accepteren.

items.title: Reconstitution d’adresses électroniques professionnelles : quels sont vos droits ?
items.summary: Lorsque vos données personnelles sont accessibles sur Internet, elles peuvent être récupérées par des organismes pour reconstituer votre adresse électronique professionnelle, notamment pour faire de la prospection. La reconstitution d’adresse électronique doit respecter le RGPD afin d’être légale. La CNIL fait le point sur vos droits.

items.title: Reconstitution d’adresses électroniques professionnelles : dans quel cadre est-ce autorisé ?
items.summary: La reconstitution d’adresses électroniques professionnelles à partir de données accessibles en ligne est utilisée pour contacter des interlocuteurs, notamment dans le cadre de la prospection. Elle est encadrée par le RGPD et ne peut reposer sur l’intérêt légitime que si certaines conditions sont remplies.

items.title: Norwegian DPA fines Xandr EUR 8 600 000 for unlawful processing of personal data
items.summary: Background information Date of final decision: 2 October 2026 National case Controller: Xandr Inc. Legal References: Article 6 (Lawfulness of processing), Article 9 (Processing of special categories of personal data) Decision: Administrative fine Key words: Fines, Basic principles, Marketing, Online platforms Summary of the Decision Origin of the case The case started in 2020 when the Norwegian Consumer Council lodged a complaint against the advertising technology company Xandr (at the time AppNexus, now a part of Microsoft) with the Norwegian DPA (Data Protection Authority). The case concerns real-time bidding in Grindr, a location-based dating app aimed at gay, bi, trans and queer people. Key Findings The Norwegian DPA has found it proven by clear preponderance of probability that Xandr processed Grindr users’ personal data, at least the fact that individuals were using Grindr, their advertising ID and IP addresses, during real-time bidding. These are personal data under Article 4(1) GDPR and data concerning sexual orientation under Article 9(1) GDPR. Xandr is considered a joint controller for the processing, both as supply-side and demand-side platform. Since the data were special category personal data, explicit consent under Article 9(2)(a) was the relevant legal basis for the processing. Xandr did not obtain consent itself, but relied on Grindr’s consent, which were invalid under Articles 4(11) and 7 GDPR. The DPA holds that accountability cannot be outsourced; each joint controller must independently verify that consent is valid and covers its own processing. The infringements were at least negligent. In light of the fact that the infringements concern some of the most central provisions in the GDPR, including sensitive data, the Norwegian DPA regards the infringements of high seriousness. items.title: EDPB publishes statement on the data protection challenges of smart glasses
items.summary: Brussels, 13 October – During its latest plenary, the EDPB has adopted statement on smart glasses and published the report “The connected gaze. Video recording, surveillance and administering evidence in the age of smart glasses” *, developed in the context of the Support Pool of Expert (SPE) programme **. As smart glasses become widely available and more frequently used, they raise significant questions for the protection of individuals’ personal data and rights and freedoms even if they create new opportunities for communication, assistance, and innovation. “These devices look like ordinary glasses, but they include cameras and microphones and are connected to the internet. This raises serious privacy concerns, as individuals may be recorded without their knowledge. The risks are even greater in sensitive environments—such as hospitals, schools, or workplaces—and when recordings are shared on social networks. And of course, children are especially at risk when using these glasses or when they are filmed.“ EDPB Chair, Anu Talus The EDPB’s text is an initial statement which provides preliminary guidance to users, manufacturers and service providers while increasing awareness about the risks these devices pose. Shared responsibility The user’s responsibility for processing personal data under the GDPR depends on the way they use their smart glasses. For example, if this involves sharing a photo or video on a public social media account, or if smart glasses are used as part of official, professional, or political activities, the user would be considered a data controller . However, if the user shares a photo or records a video of family members or friends, or if they use the device for personal translation purposes in a private context, this would be considered a purely personal activity for which the GDPR would not apply (household exemption). items.title: Italian DPA fines Wind Tre EUR 16 700 000 for unlawful telemarketing and data protection infringements

Legal Reference(s): Article 5 (Principles relating to processing of personal data), Article 6 (Lawfulness of processing), Article 12 (Transparent information, communication and modalities for the exercise of the rights of the data subject), Article 15 (Right to access by the data subject), Article 21 (Right to object), Article 24 (Responsibility of the controller), Article 25 (Data protection by design and by default) and Article 32 (Security of processing) Decision: Administrative fine, Definitive ban on data processing, Compliance order Website topics: Data subjects rights, Basic principles, Legal basis, Marketing Summary of the Decision Origin of the case The Italian Data Protection Authority (DPA) carried out an investigation into Wind Tre S.p.A. following numerous complaints and reports from individuals concerning unsolicited promotional contacts and the activation of contracts and services without their knowledge. The investigation also concerned the effectiveness of the measures adopted by the company to ensure compliance with data protection rules throughout its sales network and to manage data subjects’ requests. The Italian Authority examined, in particular, the processing carried out for telemarketing purposes, the procedures used to conclude contracts through sales partners and the technical and organisational measures implemented by Wind Tre to prevent unlawful processing. Key Findings The Italian DPA found several infringements concerning the processing of personal data for marketing and contractual purposes. Individuals continued to receive promotional communications despite having exercised their right to object or without having given valid consent. The investigation also identified cases in which contracts were activated without the individuals’ knowledge, involving the unlawful processing of their personal data.
